name: Zeng et al. 2026 primary PE dataset: cancer vs healthy, nested cross-validation
description: Ten feature sets classified cancer vs healthy on the primary paired-end dataset; mean over 10 outer folds.

attributes.protocol: Nested cross-validation on the 420-sample primary PE dataset (ten outer and ten inner folds for n > 250), class balance by down-sampling; PCA and standardisation fitted within training folds. AUC and sensitivity at 99% specificity are summarised over the 10 outer-fold models.
attributes.version: Zeng et al. 2026, Fig. 4a-b and Source Data Fig. 4 sheets Fig.4a and Fig.4b; Methods P59-P61
limitations: Developer study: the authors produced the cfMeDIP-seq cohorts and built and ran every classifier.
Clinically diagnosed cancers, many metastatic or advanced, against healthy donors; not an intended-use screening population.
Values are summaries over the 10 cross-validation fold models; the fold-level spread is reported, not a confidence interval over samples.
Fragmentomic features are computed from cfMeDIP-enriched (methylated) fragments, not from whole-genome sequencing.

Sensitivity at 99% specificity is read within each outer fold, which holds six or seven of the 64 healthy donors, so a 99% specificity threshold allows no false positive among them (counts from the source; the resolution is Rewire arithmetic).

attributes.protocol: Each of the 10 fold models trained on the primary PE dataset scores the independent PE validation samples, which were excluded from PCA, training and tuning. LFS-previvor and LFS-survivor samples are scored post hoc and counted as cancer for sensitivity summaries.
attributes.version: Zeng et al. 2026, Fig. 4c-d and Source Data Fig. 4 sheets Fig.4c and Fig.4d; Results P28 and P32
